Theme

Latin word

grātia

grātia, grātiae f.

noun, first declension

grace, charm; favour, goodwill; one’s standing with others; a favour asked or granted; influence won by favour and connections

In this lexicon

  • charm

    the recommended word · classical · Prop. 1.2.29: ūnica nec dēsit jūcundīs grātia verbīs (Lewis & Short); Ov. M. 7.44: grātia fōrmae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150

  • favour

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 1.14.7: cum aliquō in grātiam redīre (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.9.3: grātiā et largītiōne … plūrimum poterat; Traupman 313

  • favour

    also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 3.5.63: ab eō petītō grātiam istam (Lewis & Short); Traupman 98: grātiam ab aliquō petere; Traupman 313

  • influence

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.63.1: quantum grātiā, auctōritāte, pecūniā valent; Caes. BG 1.9.3: grātiā et largītiōne … plūrimum poterat; Traupman 154; Traupman 332
